newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks end higher but off day-highs.
newsitem.headline: German stocks end higher but off day-highs.

text.p: German shares closed bourse trade off day-highs but firmer on Monday following the stronger dollar and Friday's 1.58 percent gain on Wall Street.
The DAX-30 index of leading German shares closed 22.04 points up at 2,881.32, after earlier hitting a session high of 2,899.40. March DAX futures were up 32.0 points at 2,914.0.

Shares had earlier breached the 2,900 level in pre-bourse electronic trade but fell back again with dealers saying a public holiday in the southern state of Bavaria, home to a number of large banks, was holding back dealing volumes.

"People are also looking to restructure their portfolios a bit for the year ahead and I wouldn't be surprised if there was now some form of consolidation," one dealer said, referring to recent strong gains in line with the U.S. share market.
Diversified utility Veba AG was one of the strongest gainers, rising 2.15 marks to 91 after it confirmed newspaper reports that it had made a purchase to boost its cable television activities.

The group said in a statement that its Vebacom joint venture had bought cable TV group Urbana Systemtechnick in a deal which will increase its share of the cable TV market in Germany from the current seven percent to 10 percent.
Elsewhere, most activity was seen in the automotive sector, where a number of stocks were boosted by positive news emerging on the sector from the Detroit Motor Show.

Daimler-Benz gained 2.75 marks to 108.30 after its Mercedes unit, which accounts for most of parent company profits, told journalists in Detroit it expected to have beaten its 1996 north American sales target of 85,000 vehicles and saw 1997 U.S. sales at over 100,000 units.
Volkswagen was up 15 marks to 652.00 as dealers said they were confident of more data suggesting strong growth in the sector over the rest of the week.
VW was also boosted by a report it was planning this year to build a new "mini-car" to compete in the small-car market, dealer said.
German employment, gross domestic product (GDP) and new orders data due later in the week will however be studied closely for clues to the strength of any economic recovery.
